newsitem.title: GERMANY: Lebed accuses NATO of failing to change with times.
newsitem.headline: Lebed accuses NATO of failing to change with times.

text.p: Russia's Alexander Lebed, in comments on the eve of his visit to NATO headquarters, accused the western alliance of failing to adapt to the realities of the post-Cold War era.
"The threat supposedly posed by the Soviet Union and the Warsaw pact five or ten years ago no longer exists," the Kremlin's security chief told the German news magazine Der Spiegel.
"But NATO formulates and realises its aims and tasks just as it did before."

Lebed, a retired paratroop general, said in the interview, released on Saturday ahead of its publication on Monday, that the NATO's planned expansion to include Moscow's former satellites in east and central Europe was "unacceptable" for Russia.
Enlargement, he said, would change Russia geopolitical situation.

Lebed, who is due to visit NATO's Brussels headquarters on Monday, stopped short of remarks reported in a British newspaper last month, which quoted him as saying German and U.S. industrial interests would suffer if the expansion went ahead.

But he cautioned: "To tell the superpower Russia that NATO's expansion process was inevitable and has nothing to do with us... I'm no diplomat but I'd advise anyone to think extremely carefully before saying something like that."
